summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for MRSA bacteremia originating from her left femoral dialysis catheter. She presented with malaise, weakness, and catheter site pain. The infected catheter was removed, and a temporary line was placed. A stent was successfully inserted to treat underlying IVC stenosis. She experienced transient hyperkalemia requiring urgent dialysis but stabilized. Blood cultures cleared, and she completed a line holiday before receiving a new right femoral tunneled dialysis catheter. Her antibiotics were continued, warfarin was adjusted, and HIV medication adherence was addressed. She was discharged to extended care to complete her six-week vancomycin course with plans for ongoing support.
